brief.headline: You're 1.36% of their sales — use that to win faster payment terms and free up ₹1.24 Cr cash for FDC

priceAsk.summary: Hold the line on price; no increase
priceAsk.basis: We already pay market-fair rates (market asking ₹60–81/kg, typical ₹66–73/kg). They keep only 2.3% profit, so a big price cut risks our supply. Focus the ask on payment terms instead.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to immediate payment (pay on receipt) in exchange for better service or a small rebate
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying immediately instead of in 30 days frees up ₹1.24 Cr cash for us to use elsewhere

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji is financially weak — they score D (21/100) health, keep only 2.3% as profit, and owe 2.25 times their own cash (₹238.85 Cr debt). But we are a big customer: our ₹15.03 Cr is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr sales. That gives us real leverage to ask for better terms without breaking them. Their tight cash position means they'll value faster payment highly — offer it in trade for a service upgrade or a small rebate, not a steep price cut that could hurt supply.

evidence.point: We are a significant customer to them
evidence.figure: Our spend ₹15.03 Cr is 1.36% of their revenue ₹1102.11 Cr

evidence.point: They have very thin profit margins

evidence.figure: Debt to equity 2.25x, total debt ₹238.85 Cr

evidence.point: Their overall financial health is poor
Our price sits in the fair market range
Paying them immediately frees up working cash for us
evidence.figure: ₹1.24 Cr freed if we move to immediate payment

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch maker, health B (62/100), ₹2359.06 Cr revenue — a strong drop-in alternate for dextrose; qualify them to pressure Sayaji and hedge supply risk

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, health C (57/100), ₹821.13 Cr revenue — growing capacity in dextrose; a credible second source

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller making anhydrous dextrose (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; health D (27/100), ₹365.39 Cr revenue; confirm IP monograph before switching

risks: Their weak finances (D health score, 2.25x debt) mean pushing too hard on price could destabilize our supply — focus the ask on payment terms and service, not a steep discount
We already pay their best price (₹66.48/KG is our floor), so there's no gap to close — any saving must come from terms, volume rebates or faster delivery
Their thin 2.3% profit margin leaves little room to absorb cost; if we demand a cut, have Gulshan or Sanstar ready to quote as backup
Paying them immediately instead of in 30 days frees ₹1.24 Cr for us, but only do it in exchange for a concrete benefit (rebate, priority slots, tighter specs) — not as a favour
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're an important partner — we spend ₹15.03 Cr a year with you, over 1% of your sales — so let's talk about how we can both win: we'll pay you faster if you can sharpen the commercial terms or guarantee us priority supply.
